title: Run Length Expand Text
description: `s` is a compressed text made of pairs: a lowercase letter followed by a digit `1`-`9` telling how many times that letter is repeated. Return the full text.
constraints: odd positions hold lowercase letters, even positions hold digits 1-9 (counting from 1)

title: Odd Even Slot Checksum
description: Take the values at even indices (`0, 2, 4, ...`) of `a` and put them back in those same slots in ascending order; take the values at odd indices and put them back in those slots in descending order. Return `1*b1 + 2*b2 + ...` where `b` is the resulting array.

title: Spreadsheet Column Label
description: Spreadsheet columns are labelled `A, B, ..., Z, AA, AB, ..., AZ, BA, ...`. Return the label of column number `n` (counting from `1`).
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Reverse Letters Keep Others
description: Reverse the order of the letters in `s` but leave every other character (digits, spaces, `-`, `.`, `,`) in its original position. Return the result.
constraints: s has lowercase and uppercase letters, digits, spaces and the characters - . ,

title: Sentence Word Order Reverse
description: `s` is a sentence of words separated by single spaces. Return the sentence with the order of the words reversed (the letters inside each word keep their order).

examples.explanation: The reversed sentence is blue is sky the.

constraints: s has lowercase words separated by single spaces, with no leading or trailing space

title: Repeated Value Count
description: Return how many different values appear at least twice in `a`.

title: Fewest Binary Digit Numbers
description: Call a positive integer a binary-digit number if every digit in its decimal form is `0` or `1` (such as `1`, `10`, `11`, `101`). Return the fewest binary-digit numbers (repeats allowed) whose sum is exactly `n`.
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Generation Member Count
description: A family tree has members `0..n-1` with `n = par.length + 1`; member `i + 1` is a child of member `par[i]` (with `par[i] <= i`), and member `0` is the founder (generation `0`, their children are generation `1`, and so on). Return how many members belong to generation `L`.

title: Diamond Row Width
description: A diamond of stars has `2n - 1` rows: row `1` has one star, each next row has two more stars until the middle row `n`, and then the rows shrink back to one star. Return the number of stars in row `r` (rows counted from `1`).
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Merged Unique Length
description: `a` and `b` are both sorted in non-decreasing order. Return how many different values appear in `a` and `b` together.

title: Pattern Occurrence Count
description: Return how many positions of `s` start an occurrence of `p` (occurrences may overlap).
constraints: s and p have only lowercase letters

title: Spreadsheet Label To Number
description: Spreadsheet columns are labelled `A, B, ..., Z, AA, AB, ...`. Return the column number (counting from `1`) of the label `s`.
constraints: s has only uppercase letters A-Z

title: Right Leaders Count
description: An element is a right leader if it is strictly greater than every element to its right (the last element is always a right leader). Return the number of right leaders in `a`.

title: Most Frequent Values Count
description: Return how many different values of `a` occur as often as the most frequent value does (the most frequent value itself is included).

examples.explanation: 2 values tie for the highest frequency.
1 values tie for the highest frequency.

title: Typed Texts Equal With Backspace
description: Two texts are typed on a keyboard where the `#` key deletes the previous character (and does nothing on an empty text). Return `true` if `s` and `t` end up as the same text.
constraints: s and t have lowercase letters and #

title: Longest Sentence Word Count
description: `s` is a paragraph of lowercase words separated by single spaces. Sentences end with `.`, `!` or `?`. Return the number of words in the sentence with the most words.

examples.input: s = "this is one. short! is it a question?"

constraints: s has lowercase letters, spaces and sentence terminators . ! ?; it contains at least one word

args: this is one. short! is it a question?
a. b c. d e f.

title: Elements Without Multiple Partner
description: Return how many elements `x` of `a` have no element equal to `x * k` anywhere in `a`.

title: Missing Letter Count
description: Return how many of the 26 letters of the English alphabet do not appear in `s`, ignoring case.
constraints: s has letters (both cases), digits and spaces

args: Pack my box with five dozen liquor jugs

title: Twin Prime Pairs Upto N
description: A twin prime pair is two primes that differ by `2`, such as `(3, 5)`. Return how many twin prime pairs `(p, p + 2)` have both numbers at most `n`.
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Fibonacci Even Sum Upto N
description: Consider the Fibonacci terms `1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, ...` (each term is the sum of the previous two). Return the sum of the even terms that are at most `n`.
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Strong Number Check
description: A number is strong if it equals the sum of the factorials of its digits (for example `145 = 1! + 4! + 5!`). Return `true` if `n` is strong.
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Automorphic Number Check
description: A number is automorphic if its square ends with the number itself (`25 * 25 = 625` ends with `25`). Return `true` if `n` is automorphic.
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Palindromic Number Count In Range
description: Return how many integers from `l` to `r` (both included) read the same forwards and backwards in decimal.
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Alternating Series Sum
description: Return the sum of the first `n` terms of the series `1 - 2 + 3 - 4 + 5 - ...`.
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: First Non-Repeating Letter Index
description: Return the index of the first letter of `s` that occurs exactly once in `s`, or `-1` if there is none.

title: Values Appearing Once Count
description: Return how many values appear exactly once in `a`.

title: Best Contiguous Sum
description: Return the largest sum of a non-empty contiguous part of `a`.

title: First Index In Sorted
description: `a` is sorted in non-decreasing order. Return the smallest index at which `t` occurs in `a`, or `-1` if `t` does not occur.

title: Daily Steps Target
description: You need `goal` steps in total and have already walked `done` steps. Return the smallest whole number of steps you must walk on each of the remaining `days` days (the same number every day) to reach the goal. Return `0` if the goal is already reached.
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Octal To Binary Text
description: `s` is a number written in octal (digits `0`-`7`). Return the same number written in binary, without leading zeros (`0` stays `0`).

title: Hanoi Total Moves
description: In the Tower of Hanoi with `n` disks, return the smallest number of moves needed to transfer the whole tower to another rod, one disk at a time, never putting a larger disk on a smaller one.

examples.explanation: The smallest number of moves is 7.
The smallest number of moves is 1.

constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Factorial Modulo
description: Return `n!` (the product `1 * 2 * ... * n`, with `0! = 1`) modulo `m`.
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Range AND Value
description: Return the bitwise AND of all integers from `l` to `r`, both included.

examples.explanation: The AND of the range is 4.
The AND of the range is 0.

constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Next Power Of Two Sum
description: For every element, find the smallest power of two (`1, 2, 4, 8, ...`) that is at least as large as it. Return the sum of these powers.

title: Add Reversed Digit Lists
description: Two non-negative numbers are stored as lists of decimal digits with the least significant digit first (`[3, 4, 2]` is `243`). Return their sum as a normal decimal string.
constraints: every digit is 0-9 (leading zeros are allowed)

title: Shortest Path With Keys
description: `s` is a grid whose rows are separated by single spaces. `@` is the start, `.` is a free cell, `#` is a wall, a lowercase letter `a..f` is a key (each key appears at most once) and an uppercase letter `A..F` is a lock that can be entered only after the matching key has been picked up. You move one cell up, down, left or right per step, and stepping on a key picks it up. Return the fewest steps needed to pick up every key in the grid (`0` if there are none), or `-1` if that is impossible.
constraints: 1 <= rows, columns <= 30 and rows have equal length
exactly one `@`; characters are from `@.#a-fA-F`; each lowercase letter appears at most once

title: Word Search Path Count
description: `s` is a letter grid whose rows are separated by single spaces. A path spells `w` if it visits `w.length` cells where each next cell is the neighbour (up, down, left or right) of the previous one, no cell is used twice and the letters read, in order, equal `w`. Return the number of different paths that spell `w`.
constraints: 1 <= rows, columns <= 6 and rows have equal length

title: Largest Block After Column Reorder
description: A table with `cols` columns holds `0`s and `1`s row by row in `g`. You may rearrange the columns in any order (whole columns move together). Return the area of the largest rectangle made only of `1`s that can be obtained.
constraints: 1 <= cols and 1 <= g.length <= 1000000 and g.length is a multiple of cols

title: Kth Smallest Row Pick Sum
description: A table with `cols` columns is stored row by row in `g`. Choose exactly one element from every row and add them up. Over all possible choices (choices that use different columns count separately, even when the sums are equal), return the `k`-th smallest sum, counting from `1`.
constraints: 1 <= cols <= 40, 1 <= rows <= 40 and g.length = rows * cols

title: Profit With Cooldown And Fee
description: `p[i]` is a share price on day `i`. You may hold at most one share. Buying costs `p[i]`; selling returns `p[i]` but also costs a fixed `fee` per sale. After a sale you must rest for the whole next day (no buying on the day right after a sale). You can trade as often as you like. Return the greatest total profit (`0` if you never trade).

title: Snake And Ladder Fewest Throws
description: A board has cells `1..n`. You start on cell `1` and each throw of a die moves you forward by `1` to `6` cells; a throw that would go beyond cell `n` is not allowed. `j` lists snakes and ladders as flat pairs `(from, to)`: if you land on cell `from` you are immediately moved to cell `to` (a jump never leads onto another jump cell). Return the fewest throws needed to stand on cell `n`, or `-1` if it cannot be done.
constraints: 2 <= n <= 100000 and j.length is even, at most 200000
each `from` is in 2..n-1 and appears once; each `to` is in 1..n and is not a `from` cell

title: Fewest Insertions To Palindrome
description: You may insert letters anywhere in `s`. Return the fewest insertions that turn `s` into a palindrome.

title: Longest Bitonic Subsequence
description: Return the length of the longest subsequence of `a` that first strictly increases and then strictly decreases. The increasing part or the decreasing part may be empty, so a strictly increasing subsequence, a strictly decreasing one, or a single element also qualifies.

title: Maximin Grid Path
description: A table with `cols` columns is stored row by row in `g`. Walk from the top-left cell to the bottom-right cell, moving one cell up, down, left or right at a time. The score of a walk is the smallest value among all cells it visits (both end cells included). Return the largest score any walk can have.
constraints: 1 <= cols and 1 <= g.length <= 1000000 and g.length is a multiple of cols

title: Island Count After Additions Sum
description: A `R x C` map starts as all water. `ops` lists cells as flat pairs `(row, col)`; for each pair, in order, that cell becomes land (a cell that already is land stays land). After every operation count the islands, where an island is a group of land cells linked by up, down, left or right neighbours. Return the sum of these counts over all operations, modulo `1000000007`.
constraints: 1 <= R, C <= 100000 and 2 <= ops.length <= 200000, ops.length is even

title: Non-Decreasing Digit Numbers Count
description: Count the integers `x` with `1 <= x <= n` whose decimal digits never decrease from left to right (for example `1223` and `7`, but not `1320`).
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Two Non-Overlapping Windows Sum
description: Choose one block of exactly `L` consecutive elements and one block of exactly `M` consecutive elements from `a` so that the blocks do not share any position (either block may come first). Return the largest possible total of the two blocks.
constraints: 1 <= L, M and L + M <= a.length <= 100000

title: Subarrays With Bounded Maximum
description: Return the number of non-empty contiguous parts of `a` whose largest element lies between `lo` and `hi` (both included).

title: Distinct Subset Sum Count
description: Every subset of `a` (including the empty one) has a sum. Return how many different sums occur.

title: Shortest Common Supersequence Length
description: Return the length of the shortest string that contains both `a` and `b` as subsequences.

title: Largest Divisible Chain Subset
description: `a` holds distinct positive integers. Pick as many of them as you can so that for any two picked numbers one divides the other. Return how many you can pick.
constraints: 1 <= a[i] <= 1000000000 and all values are different

title: Increasing Subsequences Of Length K Count
description: Count the subsequences of `a` that have exactly `k` elements and are strictly increasing (subsequences taken from different positions count separately even if they look alike). Return the count modulo `1000000007`.

title: Gift Packing K Boxes Max Distinct
description: Gifts are in a row, gift `i` having type `a[i]`. Cut the row into exactly `k` non-empty consecutive boxes. A box scores the number of different gift types inside it. Return the largest total score.

title: Cheapest Array Clearing
description: You must turn every element of `a` into `0`. Operation A picks one element and sets it to `0` at a cost of `x`. Operation B picks a contiguous part in which every element is at least `1` and subtracts `1` from each of them, at a cost of `y`. You may use the operations in any order and any number of times. Return the smallest total cost.

title: Best Block Sum With K Skips
description: Pick a contiguous part of `a` and then skip (leave out of the sum) at most `k` of its elements, but at least one element must stay counted. Return the largest sum you can get.

title: Bounded Knapsack Large Counts
description: Item `i` weighs `w[i]`, is worth `v[i]`, and at most `c[i]` copies of it are available. Choose how many copies of each item to take so that the total weight does not exceed `cap` and the total value is as large as possible. Return that value.

title: Pairs With AND Zero Count
description: Count the pairs of positions `i < j` for which `a[i] & a[j] = 0` (bitwise AND).

title: Maximum Subset XOR
description: Choose any subset of `a` (possibly empty) and XOR its elements together. Return the largest value that can be obtained.

title: Shortest Subarrays For Max OR Total
description: For every start position `i`, let `m_i` be the bitwise OR of `a[i], a[i+1], ..., a[n-1]`. Find the shortest part that starts at `i` and whose OR equals `m_i`, and take its length. Return the sum of these lengths over all start positions, modulo `1000000007`.

title: Split Gifts Smallest Heaviest Box
description: Gift `i` weighs `a[i]`. Pack the row of gifts, in order, into exactly `k` non-empty boxes of consecutive gifts. Return the smallest possible weight of the heaviest box.

title: Fibonacci Spiral Cell Value
description: An `R x C` grid is filled with the Fibonacci numbers `1, 1, 2, 3, 5, ...` in clockwise spiral order, starting at the top-left cell and first moving right. Return the number stored in the cell at row `r`, column `c` (counting from `0`), modulo `1000000007`.

title: Nested Repeat Character At
description: `s` is encoded as follows: `k[x]` means the decoded form of `x` repeated `k` times, and letters stand for themselves; encodings can be nested and concatenated (`2[a3[bc]]d` decodes to `abcbcbcabcbcbcd`). Return the `k`-th character (counting from `1`) of the decoded string. The decoded string may be far too long to build.
constraints: s is a valid encoding, every repeat count is between 1 and 1000, and 1 <= k <= the decoded length

title: Smallest Topological Position
description: A directed graph has nodes `0..n-1` and edges given as flat pairs `(from, to)`; an edge means `from` must come before `to`. Among all orderings of all nodes that respect every edge, take the lexicographically smallest one (comparing node numbers). Return the position (counting from `0`) of node `x` in it, or `-1` if no valid ordering exists.
constraints: 1 <= n <= 100000 and 0 <= edges.length <= 200000 and edges.length is even

title: Fewest Swaps To Sort Three Values
description: `a` contains only the values `0`, `1` and `2`. In one move you swap any two elements (they need not be neighbours). Return the fewest moves needed to sort `a` in non-decreasing order.

examples.explanation: The fewest number of swaps is 2.
The fewest number of swaps is 0.

title: Equal Pairs With Gap
description: Return the number of pairs of indices `i < j` with `a[i] == a[j]` and `j - i >= k`.

title: Least Frequently Used Hit Count
description: A cache holds at most `cap` distinct keys. Each request in `seq` that finds its key in the cache is a hit and raises that key's use count by one. A request for a missing key is a miss: if the cache is full, first evict the key with the smallest use count (ties: the key whose most recent use is the oldest), then store the new key with use count `1`. Return the number of hits.

title: Descendants At Generation Total
description: A family tree has members `0..n-1` with `n = par.length + 1`; member `i + 1` is a child of member `par[i]` (with `par[i] <= i`). `queries` lists questions as flat pairs `(x, g)`: how many descendants of member `x` are exactly `g` generations below `x` (`g = 1` means children, `g = 2` grandchildren, ...)? Return the sum of all answers, modulo `1000000007`.

examples.explanation: The answers add up to 6 modulo 1000000007.
The answers add up to 0 modulo 1000000007.

constraints: 0 <= par.length <= 100000 and 2 <= queries.length <= 200000 and queries.length is even
0 <= par[i] <= i, 0 <= x <= par.length and 1 <= g <= 100000

title: Dotted Quad Split Count
description: Count the ways to cut the digit string `s` into exactly four non-empty parts that could be the four numbers of an IPv4 address: each part is a number from `0` to `255` written without leading zeros (the part `0` itself is allowed).

title: Taxi Dispatch Top Earner
description: Taxis stand on a straight road at positions `starts[i]` (all free at time `0`). `requests` lists bookings as flat triples `(time, pickup, drop)` sorted by time. For each booking, among the taxis that are free at that time (a taxi is free from the moment its last trip ends), the one closest to `pickup` is sent (ties: the smaller taxi number); if no taxi is free the booking is dropped. A trip takes `|taxiPosition - pickup| + |drop - pickup|` time units, the taxi ends at `drop`, and earns `|drop - pickup|`. Return the number of the taxi with the highest total earnings (ties: the smaller number).
constraints: 1 <= starts.length <= 100 and 3 <= requests.length <= 30000 and requests.length is a multiple of 3
0 <= starts[i], pickup, drop <= 1000000 and times are non-decreasing, 0 <= time <= 1000000

title: Inventory Order Replay Revenue
description: A shop sells items `0..m-1`; `prices[i]` is the price of one unit of item `i`, and every item starts with no stock. `ops` lists events as flat triples `(type, item, qty)`. Type `0` adds `qty` units to the stock of `item`. Type `1` is a customer order for `qty` units: the shop ships as many as it has (up to `qty`) and the customer pays the price for each shipped unit. Return the total revenue, modulo `1000000007`.
constraints: 1 <= prices.length <= 1000 and 3 <= ops.length <= 30000 and ops.length is a multiple of 3
1 <= prices[i], qty <= 1000000, type is 0 or 1 and 0 <= item < prices.length

title: Kth Distinct In Two Sorted
description: `a` and `b` are sorted in non-decreasing order. Consider the different values that appear in `a` or `b`, listed in increasing order. Return the `k`-th of them (counting from `1`), or `-1` if there are fewer than `k`.

title: Frequency Sort Checksum
description: Rearrange `a` so that values that occur more often come first; values with the same number of occurrences are ordered by increasing value, and equal values stay together. If the rearranged array is `b`, return `1*b1 + 2*b2 + ...` (positions counted from `1`) modulo `1000000007`.

title: Distinct Pair Sum Count
description: Return the number of different value pairs `(x, y)` with `x <= y` and `x + y = t` that can be taken from two different positions of `a` (two pairs are the same if they have the same `x` and `y`).

title: Longest Stretch Without Repeats
description: Return the length of the longest substring of `s` in which no letter appears twice.

title: Largest Concatenated Number
description: Join all the numbers of `a` one after another, in any order you like, into a single decimal string. Return the largest number that can be formed, as a string (`0` if every number is `0`).

title: Fewest Platforms Needed
description: Train `i` arrives at time `arr[i]` and leaves at time `dep[i]` (with `arr[i] < dep[i]`). It occupies a platform during `[arr[i], dep[i])`, so a platform freed at time `t` can be used by a train arriving at time `t`. Return the smallest number of platforms that lets every train use a platform for its whole stay.

title: Right Leaders Sum
description: An element is a right leader if it is strictly greater than every element to its right (the last element is always one). Return the sum of the right leaders of `a`.

title: Next Digit Permutation
description: `s` is a string of digits. Return the smallest rearrangement of its digits that is strictly larger than `s` when read as a string of the same length, or `-1` if `s` already is the largest arrangement.

title: Merged Rows Checksum
description: A table with `cols` columns is stored row by row in the flat array `g`; every row is sorted in non-decreasing order. Merge all rows into one sorted sequence, dropping repeated values so each value appears once. If that sequence is `u`, return `1*u1 + 2*u2 + ...` modulo `1000000007`.
constraints: 1 <= cols and 1 <= g.length <= 1000000 and g.length is a multiple of cols
-1000000000 <= g[i] <= 1000000000 and every row is sorted

title: Fewest Additions For Multiple Pairs
description: You want to split `a` into pairs so that the sum of every pair is a multiple of `k`. You may insert extra integers of your choice into `a` first. Return the fewest integers you must insert so that such a split exists.

title: Smallest Prime Factor Sum
description: For each integer `m` from `2` to `n`, take its smallest prime divisor. Return the sum of these values modulo `1000000007` (`0` if `n < 2`).
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Longest Collatz Start Below N
description: The Collatz walk from `s` repeats: if the number is even halve it, otherwise replace it with `3*x + 1`, until it reaches `1`. Among the starts `s = 1, 2, ..., n - 1`, return the one whose walk takes the most steps (the smallest such `s` on ties).
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Fewest Bracket Insertions
description: `s` contains only `(` and `)`. You may insert brackets anywhere. Return the fewest insertions that make `s` a correctly balanced bracket string.

title: Rotate Matrix Checksum
description: A table with `cols` columns is stored row by row in `g`. Rotate the table by 90 degrees clockwise and read the rotated table row by row into a flat list `f`. Return `1*f1 + 2*f2 + ...` modulo `1000000007`.
constraints: 1 <= cols and 1 <= g.length <= 1000000 and g.length is a multiple of cols

title: Most Common Digit Upto N
description: Write the numbers `1, 2, ..., n` one after another into a single long string of digits. Return the digit that appears most often in it (the smallest such digit if several tie).
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Closest Pair Sum
description: Among all sums `a[i] + a[j]` with `i < j`, return the one that is nearest to `t`. If two sums are equally near, return the smaller sum.

title: Triplets Sum Divisible By K Count
description: Count the index triples `i < j < l` for which `a[i] + a[j] + a[l]` is divisible by `k`. Return the count modulo `1000000007`.

title: Fewest Range Decrements
description: In one operation you choose a contiguous part of `a` and subtract `1` from every element in it. All elements of `a` are non-negative. Return the fewest operations that turn every element into `0`.

title: Fewest Days To Make Bouquets
description: Flower `i` of a row blooms on day `bloom[i]` and stays in bloom afterwards. A bouquet needs `k` neighbouring flowers that are all in bloom, and a flower can be used in only one bouquet. Return the earliest day on which `m` bouquets can be made, or `-1` if it is impossible.

title: Smallest Uniform Digit Base
description: Return the smallest base `b >= 2` in which all digits of `n` are the same (for example `7` is `111` in base `2`). Bases larger than `n` are not considered, and `n >= 3` guarantees that an answer exists.
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Knapsack With Item Limit
description: Item `i` weighs `w[i]` and is worth `v[i]`. Choose at most `k` different items whose total weight does not exceed `cap`, to maximise the total value. Return that value.
constraints: 1 <= w.length = v.length <= 100 and 1 <= cap <= 1000 and 1 <= k <= 100

title: Max Subarray Sum Length Bounds
description: Return the largest sum of a contiguous part of `a` whose length is at least `lo` and at most `hi`. A part of that length always exists.

title: Pointer Chain Cycle Start
description: Cell `i` of `a` holds the number of the cell that comes after it (`0 <= a[i] < a.length`). Walk from cell `0` following these pointers forever. The walk must eventually loop; return the first cell of that loop, meaning the first cell that the walk visits twice.

title: Covered Length Of Segments
description: `s` lists segments of a number line as flat pairs `(l, r)` with `l < r`; a segment covers the stretch from `l` to `r`. Return the total length of the number line covered by at least one segment (overlaps are counted once).

title: Subarrays With Sum K Count
description: Return the number of non-empty contiguous parts of `a` whose elements add up to exactly `k`.

title: Best Two-Box Distinct Split
description: Gifts are laid in a row, gift `i` having type `a[i]`. Cut the row at one place into two non-empty parts, a left box and a right box. The score of a cut is the number of different types in the left box plus the number of different types in the right box. Return the best possible score.

title: Range AND Queries Total
description: Each query `(l, r)` (given as flat pairs in `q`, indices counted from `0`) asks for the bitwise AND of `a[l], a[l+1], ..., a[r]`. Return the sum of the answers of all queries, modulo `1000000007`.
constraints: 1 <= a.length <= 100000 and 2 <= q.length <= 100000 and q.length is even

title: Maximum Gap In Sorted Order
description: Sort `a` and look at every pair of neighbours in the sorted order. Return the largest difference between two neighbours (`0` if all values are equal).

title: Largest Below With Distinct Digits
description: Return the largest positive integer strictly smaller than `n` whose decimal digits are all different, or `0` if there is none.
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Subarray Product Below K Count
description: All elements of `a` are positive. Count the non-empty contiguous parts of `a` whose product of elements is strictly less than `k`. Return the count modulo `1000000007`.
